A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MaxEntDP and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched reliably despite reformatting, renumbering, and expanded appendices.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original multi-goal trajectories, MuJoCo learning curves, ablations, hyperparameter studies, and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original AntMaze exploration results, DeepMind Control learning curves, and Gaussian-mixture probability-approximation tests in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The QNE objective, probability estimator, bounded-action treatment, action selection, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. However, new Appendix B states that generation uses DDPM ancestral sampling, whereas the retained Section 3.3 specifies probability-flow ODE sampling. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects a sampler change or inconsistent documentation.

E1.justification: v3 retains the original coverage and adds four AntMaze scenarios, DeepMind Control's Dog Stand, Dog Walk, and Humanoid Walk tasks, and a four-component Gaussian-mixture density-estimation test. These extend evaluation to high-dimensional maze exploration and direct probability approximation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The added DeepMind Control tests reuse SAC, MEow, and TD3; AntMaze uses SAC. CrossQ, BRO, DDiffPG, and the additional energy-model methods are discussed or cited but are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include AntMaze trajectory and state-coverage evaluation after one million interactions using dense distance-based rewards, and comparison of estimated versus known Gaussian-mixture log densities while varying T and N. These introduce distinct evaluation procedures. Settings for the retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds trajectory and state-coverage analyses comparing multimodal exploration with SAC. Appendix D.4 directly examines probability-estimation accuracy and sensitivity to diffusion steps and Monte Carlo samples. The original entropy ablation, QNE comparisons, and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report learning-curve means and standard deviations over five runs; new Figure 10 follows the same practice. No changed replication counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported. The estimator sample count N is not a repeated-run count.

E6.justification: Existing plots and table values are unchanged. New Figures 8–11 show broader AntMaze exploration than SAC, stronger returns on the two Dog tasks, and probability-approximation heatmaps. Figure 10 shows broadly similar final Humanoid Walk returns to SAC, qualifying the text's blanket outperformance statement. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The SAC results, score-estimation formulas, probability approximation, and Appendix A proofs are retained. v3 makes the inverse-sigmoid identity explicit when explaining the existing change of integration variable and refines interval notation, without substantively changing the derivation or adding a formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: diffusion policies for MaxEnt RL, Q-weighted noise estimation, numerical probability approximation, advantages over Gaussian and flow policies, and competitive performance against diffusion-based online RL.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 newly interprets imperfect probability estimates as potentially useful for curiosity-driven exploration. Appendix B adds computational, sampling-diversity, and bounded-action arguments distinguishing QNE from model-based diffusion. The original exploration interpretation and limitation concerning manually selected temperatures remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the new toy distribution's component parameters and Q(x)=log p(x) construction, plus AntMaze reward and interaction-budget details. Existing hardware, code references, architecture settings, and timing information are retained. Documentation remains inconsistent: D.4 specifies N=20 for the smaller sample setting, while Figure 11 and its caption specify N=10.

R1.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands positioning against diffusion-based energy models, discussing Sendera et al.'s diffusion samplers and explicitly acknowledging similarities to Pan et al.'s model-based diffusion before arguing distinctions. Section 4 also adds CrossQ and BRO, and D.2 cites DDiffPG as the AntMaze source. Existing related work is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include small explanatory edits, conference and author information, acknowledgements, and appendix reorganization: v1's experimental appendix is divided between implementation details and supplementary experiments, alongside a new related-work appendix.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and relocating existing displays. The first two figures exchange numbering, appendix figures and tables are reorganized, and Figures 8–11 add maze trajectories, state coverage, control-task curves, and probability heatmaps.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support by extending multimodal exploration beyond v1's two-dimensional toy and directly checking probability approximation against a known density. Additional control tasks and closer related-work comparisons also help. The gains are qualified: the new coverage and accuracy evidence is mainly qualitative, Humanoid Walk does not clearly support blanket superiority, and the sampler and N inconsistencies reduce clarity and reproducibility.
